newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end lower on surge in interest rates.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end lower on surge in interest rates.

text.p: A surge in three-month interest rates earlier on Monday helped depress Kuala Lumpur share prices on Monday, dealers said.
The key Kuala Lumpur Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks fell 2.11 points to 1,015.50, after dipping to 1,010.41 in the morning.
"There has been some short covering by the foreign funds," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
Weakness in Sime Darby and Tenaga helped to pull the index down. The two stocks contribute about 15 percent of the weightage of the Composite Index.
The three-month interbank rate was fixed at 14.9 percent in its daily morning fixing, against 11.15 on Friday. The ringgit had dipped to a 16-month low of 2.5500/10 to the dollar.

"When the (Philippines) peso fell last week, it provided a big boost to the stock market. But today the market is indecisive about which direction to go in," said the head of research at a local brokerage.
The day's most active issues were Rahman Hydraulic and KLI Holdings on news the companies were involved in a restructuring plan with each other.
Property developer KLI said on Friday it would inject its entire 60 percent stake in Malaysia Electric Corporation Bhd (MECB) into Rahman Hydraulic, also a property developer.
MECB earlier this year launched a sprawling 1,200 hectare township, focused on the manufacture of Malaysian-branded household electrical goods.
Rahman gained 55 cents to 5.60 ringgit, and KLI holdings rose eight cents to 3.04 ringgit.
Market volume stood at 241 million shares valued at 1,763 million ringgit. Losers outnumbered gainers 487 to 150.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot July contract lost 4.7 points to 1,017.7 with 1,081 lots traded. August futures rose 0.3 of a point to 1,015.7 with 30 lots traded.
